answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils expensive: each new agent must lock a refundable deposit, and an established voucher co-signs it, staking its own reputation. A fraud ring is no safe haven, since one caught fake slashes the whole chain of vouchers, so no agent is an island. Forging a thousand identities means funding a thousand deposits dug from hard shale, then forfeiting them all the moment one is exposed. The attacker's cost scales linearly with the size of the lie.
